Alex Chen: Hey all — quick question. I need to travel to India for consular stamping in ~2 weeks. Offer start is 2026-04-15. My H1B COS to Redwood was approved earlier but we filed an amendment for the new office and that amendment is still pending. Can I travel and get stamped? Will this affect my start date/payroll/benefits? :airplane:

Jae Park (People Ops): Hi Alex :wave: — thanks for flagging. A few quick notes: 1) If your COS is approved and you already have an H1B approval (I-797) then leaving the US typically means you'll need consular stamping to re-enter. 2) If the amendment is pending and it's tied to a material change (location/role), travel could complicate the amendment — Priya can confirm. 3) I-9 needs physical verification by day 1. If you're outside the US at hire we usually either delay the I-9/start date or complete I-9 when you return. 4) Payroll/benefits: we can set a flexible start date in Workday so benefits enrollment isn't lost. Can you share exact travel dates?

Priya Rao (Legal): Quick legal nuance: if your underlying COS (change of status) was approved to H1B already (you have an I-797 showing approval), leaving the US is OK but you will need consular stamping to re-enter under H1. If what’s pending is an amendment (same petition but material change like new office), leaving while the amendment is pending does not automatically void the amendment, but it can create timing/logistics issues with USCIS receipts and consulate processing. If the amendment changes location and that impacts LCA, we should avoid travel until amendment receipts are in place or coordinate with our counsel. I'm not saying don't travel — just that there is more paperwork risk and potential delays. Recommend either: a) postpone travel until amendment has an USCIS receipt, or b) proceed but accept possible extra admin/consulate questions and plan for delayed physical I-9.

Sven Müller (Hiring Manager): Thanks Priya. From the team side we're flexible on start. We can begin onboarding tasks that don't require attestation (docs, access requests, intro meetings) before your physical I-9. If you need to shift start to after your return, that's fine. Alex — what are the exact dates? Also if you want to start remotely we can create a checklist of tasks you can do pre-I-9.

Alex Chen: Travel dates 2026-03-28 to 2026-04-10. Ideally I'd still love to keep 4/15 start. If I can't get stamped in time I can push to 4/29. Also, will benefits enrollment window close if start delayed?

Jae Park (People Ops): Thanks. For benefits: we can set an effective date based on your finalized start. If you keep 4/15 and do I-9 after return, we can make a note to payroll to allow retroactive benefits effective 4/15 — but that requires coordination. I'll file the payroll note now.

Jae Park (People Ops): Action items for now:
- Alex: scan passport, I-797 approval, I-94 and send to me (encrypted) before you leave.
- Priya: confirm whether amendment receipt should be awaited (is pending amendment the kind that would block consular stamping?)
- People Ops: prepare start-date adjustment template for payroll & benefits

Priya Rao (Legal): Confirming — the amendment itself doesn't always block consular stamping but consulates will ask for current employer docs and the most recent approval/receipt. If your stamp appointment goes smoothly you should be fine. If you have any RFEs or the consulate requests more employer evidence, that can delay re-entry. If the role/location changed materially, we advise waiting for at least an amendment receipt notice. If you want, I can loop in our outside immigration counsel for a quick sign-off.

Jae Park (People Ops): Sample email I'll send to Payroll (copying you):

``` 
Subject: ADJ: Start Date / Benefits Enrollment Exception - Alex Chen - ROLE
Body: Alex Chen (candidate) traveling 3/28-4/10 for consular stamping. Hiring manager requests start date 4/15. I-9 cannot be completed while candidate is outside US; request payroll to allow benefits enrollment effective 4/15 pending completion of I-9 on first business day back. Please hold benefits window and confirm any retro payroll implications.
```

Sven Müller (Hiring Manager): That looks good. Alex — ok if I approve the temporary remote onboarding checklist now?

Alex Chen: Yes please, that would be great. Also — is there guidance for I-9 completion if I land back and need to visit a local HR authorized representative? Do we have partners in India/consulate who can act as authorized reps?

Priya Rao (Legal): I-9 law requires physical inspection in the US. We cannot accept overseas verification for Form I-9. Authorized representative model can be used (we appoint someone to inspect on our behalf), but that person must inspect documents in the US; using an overseas agent is risky and not standard. So we should plan to complete I-9 once you're physically back in the US before starting work that requires employment authorization verification.

Jae Park (People Ops): Noted. Alex — we'll: 1) hold the official I-9 until you return, 2) provision accounts with time-limited access where needed, 3) confirm benefits window still open after payroll note. I'll loop in BenefitsBot to create the enrollment exception ticket.

BenefitsBot: Ticket created: BNFT-2026-4473 — Benefits hold requested for Alex Chen, effective date 2026-04-15 pending I-9.

Alex Chen: Awesome, thank you all. Please cc me on any payroll note. I'll upload scans tonight. :thumbsup:

Jae Park (People Ops): Will do. Sending payroll note and looping counsel for one quick check. If anything changes we’ll update here. Safe travels! :airplane:
